<reflection>
The second experiment (low catalyst) helped differentiate mechanisms based on catalyst order, but many mechanisms remain plausible with small NLL differences. The top mechanisms (M3, M5, M4) are within ~1.2 NLL, and a broader group (M6, M8, M7, M2, etc.) are within ~7 NLL. The aim for this turn is to propose an experiment that reduces uncertainty across this set, not just between the top two. Since both previous experiments had no initial product, adding product introduces a new dimension that will affect mechanisms differently based on product reversibility and product-induced deactivation. This design should be informative for many mechanisms simultaneously.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
I propose adding a moderate initial product concentration (0.2 M) while keeping substrate and catalyst at the same levels as the first experiment (S=1.0 M, cat=0.01 M). This will directly compare with run1 (no product) to assess the effect of product on kinetics. Mechanisms with reversible product formation (all candidates have this step) will show a reduced net forward rate due to the reverse reaction, but the extent of reduction depends on the equilibrium constant. Mechanisms with explicit product-induced deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) may exhibit accelerated loss of activity beyond simple reversibility. Additionally, mechanisms with product inhibition (implicit in some steps) could show different time-course shapes. By analyzing the initial rate suppression and the curvature of the product vs. time curve, we can discriminate among mechanisms that otherwise fit similarly without product. This condition avoids extreme product concentrations that might saturate the reverse reaction and collapse differences, and it complements previous experiments by probing a new regulatory factor.
</hypothesis>
